issues.detail: The Greek 'λεγων ου παραγγελια' (saying, 'no order') is rendered as 'ra mạng lịnh cấm' (issued a forbidding order). In the Greek, Jesus is quoting the Pharisees saying they gave no order; the Vietnamese makes it sound like he is describing an actual order that was issued.

The Greek 'πεπληρωκατε την ιερουσαλημ' (you have filled Jerusalem) is rendered as 'làm cho thành Giê-ru-sa-lem đầy dẫy' (made the city of Jerusalem full). While similar, the Greek uses a perfect tense indicating a completed state/action of filling, which the Vietnamese captures well enough, but the primary issue remains the introductory quote.
